title: Durable consumption and expected stock returns: Yogo (2006)
estimand: Relative risk aversion gamma in Yogo's durable-consumption model with Epstein-Zin utility, estimated by GMM from the Euler equations of the test assets, the 3-month T-bill and the intratemporal first-order condition (quarterly, 1951-2001).

parameters.name: rho
parameters.label: Elasticity of substitution between nondurables and durables

options.label: 25 size-BE/ME portfolios
options.justification: Yogo Table II column 1 (baseline). Starting values as in nlest_dur.prg: linear-model sigma, gamma and alpha, rho from the cointegration regression, beta = 0.92; first step as saved in results/FF/nlest_dur.fmt (GAUSS return code 3, Borri and Ragusa 2017).

options.label: 24 industry-by-BE/ME portfolios
options.justification: Yogo Table II column 2. Yogo's code starts this set from the saved 25-portfolio second-step estimate; its saved first-step vector equals that start (the GAUSS first step never moved).

options.label: 25 market- and HML-beta portfolios
options.justification: Yogo Table II column 3. Yogo's code starts this set from the saved 25-portfolio second-step estimate; its saved first-step vector equals that start (the GAUSS first step never moved).

options.label: All 74 portfolios
options.justification: Yogo Table II column 4. Yogo's code starts this set from the saved 25-portfolio second-step estimate; its saved first-step vector equals that start (the GAUSS first step never moved).

options.label: T-bill, test assets and FOC
options.justification: Yogo: Euler equations for the T-bill and the test assets, and the intratemporal FOC.

options.label: Without the T-bill equation
options.justification: Borri and Ragusa (2017): the T-bill moment carries the rejection, and Yogo's second-step weighting gave it about 1/10,000 of the weight of the others. The FOC still pins the scale of the SDF.

options.label: Without the FOC
options.justification: Pakos (2004) does not impose the intratemporal FOC (Yogo's appendix). Dropping both the T-bill equation and the FOC is not an option: excess-return moments do not identify beta.

options.label: Two-step
options.justification: Yogo: identity first step, then the inverse long-run covariance at the first-step vector (Hansen 1982).

options.label: Identity (one step)
options.justification: A fixed, prespecified weighting (Cochrane 2005); standard errors are the sandwich form and no J test is reported.

options.label: Iterated
options.justification: Weighting re-estimated to convergence (Hansen, Heaton and Yaron 1996).

options.label: Continuously updated
options.justification: Weighting re-estimated at every parameter value (Hansen, Heaton and Yaron 1996).

options.label: As published (GAUSS first step)
options.justification: Yogo's code path: the saved GAUSS first-step vector serves as the preliminary estimate and later steps are searched locally from it.

options.label: One local search from Yogo's start
options.justification: Each step solved by one local search from Yogo's starting values (later steps from the previous step's estimate).

options.label: Multistart (21 starts)
options.justification: Borri and Ragusa (2017): the objective has several local modes. Yogo's start plus 20 Halton points over the bounds in every step; lowest converged objective kept.

options.label: VARHAC(1), AIC
options.justification: Yogo (den Haan and Levin 1997): one lag allows for time aggregation in consumption (Hall 1988).

options.label: Newey-West, 4 lags
options.justification: Kernel alternative; 4 lags is the Newey and West (1994) rule floor(4 (T/100)^(2/9)) for T of about 200.

options.label: No autocorrelation correction
options.justification: Euler-equation errors for one-period returns are a martingale difference sequence under the null (Hansen and Singleton 1982).

options.label: Beginning of period
options.justification: Yogo, following Campbell (2003): each quarter's consumption is the flow on its first day, so the return over quarter q is paired with consumption growth and inflation from q to q+1.

options.label: End of period
options.justification: The other convention discussed by Campbell (2003): the return over quarter q is paired with consumption growth and inflation over quarter q (consumption-side series lagged one quarter).
Yogo, following Ogaki and Reinhart (1998): post-war restocking of durables before 1951.
The standard sample for book-to-market-sorted portfolios (Fama and French 1993; Lettau and Ludvigson 2001).

exclusions.reason: The published first-step vector is where GAUSS stopped, not an identity-weighted minimizer, so no estimator is defined.
Re-selecting VARHAC lag orders at every parameter value makes the CUE objective discontinuous.

reference.source: Yogo (2006, JF 61(2)) Table II column 1 (25 Fama-French portfolios): gamma 191.438 (49.868). Rebuilt from the first-step vector saved in Yogo's results/FF/nlest_dur.fmt, as agreed with the author on 2026-10-18 (two-part gate in notes/application-selection.md).

notes: Two-part reproduction gate: (1) at Yogo's saved second-step vectors the moments and VARHAC reproduce Table II J statistics and standard errors (check_published.R); (2) the preferred row reproduces gamma. Local search: projected Levenberg-Marquardt on whitened moments, identical in R and Python.
